questions.q: Why does a quantum circuit need a classical register at all?
options: Classical registers store intermediate gate operations
Measurement extracts a definite readable value from a qubit, and that value needs classical memory to be written into
Classical registers are required to apply any gate
They are only needed for multi-qubit circuits
questions.explain: A qubit's complex amplitudes can't be read directly. Measurement produces a definite classical outcome, and a classical register (or classical bit) is where that outcome is stored.

Measures every qubit in the circuit into a matching set of classical bits
Runs the circuit on AerSimulator automatically
Removes all measurements from the circuit
questions.explain: measure_all() is a convenience method that measures every qubit at once, writing results into a corresponding set of classical bits.

questions.q: What happens to a qubit's superposition when it is measured?
options: Nothing changes; superposition persists after measurement
It temporarily pauses and can be restored later
It irreversibly collapses to one definite classical outcome
It splits into two separate qubits
questions.explain: Measurement is a one-way, destructive operation: a qubit in superposition collapses to a single definite outcome, and that superposition cannot be recovered afterward.

questions.q: A Hadamard-then-measure circuit has ideal probabilities P(0)=0.5, P(1)=0.5. A real 2048-shot run gave {'0': 999, '1': 1049}. What does this result indicate?
options: The simulator has a bug
The Hadamard gate was miscalibrated
Ordinary statistical shot noise from a finite sample of a true 50/50 distribution, within about 1 percentage point of ideal
The qubit was not actually in superposition
questions.explain: 999 versus 1049 out of 2048 shots is close to, but not exactly, an even split — well within the range expected from statistical sampling noise, not evidence of an error.

questions.q: What is the correct modern code pattern to run a measured circuit on AerSimulator for 2048 shots?
options: qiskit.execute(qc, AerSimulator(), shots=2048)
AerSimulator().run(transpile(qc, backend), shots=2048).result()
qc.run(shots=2048)
AerSimulator.measure(qc, 2048)
questions.explain: The modern pattern transpiles the circuit for the target backend, then calls .run() with the shots count directly on the backend object, followed by .result().
